O1.citation: “No. One passing run is evidence, not proof” explicitly rejects proof and keeps the claim provisional until further evidence.

O2.citation: “Repeat the same case blindly 2–3 more times, using a fresh, context-free agent for every run” and “Report the pass rate”; the closing requirement applies the pass-rate bar to “all cases.”

O3.citation: Runners receive “only the case input and the target skill—never the bar,” while “a separate fresh judge” receives the artifact and case bar.

O4.citation: “Determine whether it exposed a skill defect or a bad evaluation bar. Fix only genuine skill defects, then rerun every golden case.”

O5.citation: “Only after all cases consistently clear their required pass-rate bar is a durable claim defensible”; after a justified fix, the instruction to “rerun every golden case” supplies the required after-change evidence alongside the original results.

S1.citation: Smell absent: the artifact says one passing run is “evidence, not proof.”

S2.citation: Smell absent: it permits a durable claim “only after all cases consistently clear their required pass-rate bar.”

S3.citation: Smell absent: it requires 2–3 blind repetitions and reporting “the pass rate.”

S4.citation: Smell absent: runners must “never” receive “the bar, expected result, prior artifacts, or evaluation rationale.”

S5.citation: Smell absent: it requires determining “whether it exposed a skill defect or a bad evaluation bar” before fixing “only genuine skill defects.”

rationale: The artifact treats the initial success as provisional, requires fresh blind repeated trials with case-level pass-rate bars, strictly separates runners from judges, diagnoses defects before editing, and reruns the full golden suite after justified changes. It withholds any durable guidebook claim until the repeated and post-change evidence supports it.
